cohort: 2518 patients who presented to the Urogynecology Unit at Istanbul Medical School with complaints of urinary incontinence and/or pelvic organ prolapse.
finding: The prevalence of anal incontinence among patients with urinary incontinence was 12.8%, and no significant risk factors were identified.
mod_finding: No significant relationship was found between fecal and flatus incontinence and the method of delivery.
